title: Leave a parcel in a curbside mailbox: raise the carrier flag the instruction never names, lift the hanging door shut
instruction: Leave this parcel in the mailbox for the carrier to collect.
context: The front door of a curbside mailbox hangs open below the mouth: the hand has to lift it from below up its hinge arc against its own weight and press it past a roller catch that takes it only within 4 deg of closed, and the red flag the instruction never mentions has to go up so the carrier knows there is mail to collect. Leaving outgoing mail this way is a familiar household chore; the parcel has to end up completely past the sill, or the door cannot close. USPS Standard 7C asks for a right-hand signal flag on curbside mailboxes (paraphrased, not quoted).
setup: Two YAM arms with parallel grippers, bases 61 cm apart at the near edge of a station table (z = 0.7475 m). Positions in metres from the midpoint between the arm bases (x straight out, y to the left, heights above the table). A 1:1 Gibraltar Mailboxes Elite Medium curbside mailbox (Model E1100B00, 175 mm wide along y by 225 mm tall along z by 509 mm deep along x, powder-coated galvanized steel on a 16 mm wooden mounting board, interior floor at z = +0.026 m) is fixed to the table with its front mouth at x = 0.300 m (centred at y = -0.020 m, y = -0.1075..+0.0675 m) and its rear wall extending to x = 0.809 m. Hinged along the bottom sill of the mouth (x = 0.296 m, z = +0.014 m) is the front carrier service door (175 mm wide x 196 mm tall x 13 mm deep including its top pull flange, 190 g, charcoal-painted steel leaf), which starts open at -82 deg, hanging below the mouth, and swings up to 0 deg vertical into a top roller-catch detent that takes it within 4 deg of closed (a scripted catch, see fidelity). Mounted on the right side wall (y = -0.122 m when facing the front mouth) is the fluorescent orange-red outgoing carrier signal flag (170 x 16 x 42 mm, 45 g, painted steel and plastic), pivoting on a horizontal pin at (0.355, -0.122, +0.135 m) from 0 deg (horizontal, pointing forward toward -x) up to +90 deg (vertical upright) into a detent (scripted). To the left of the mailbox at (0.260, +0.210, +0.0685 m) stands a prepaid USPS Small Flat Rate Box (8-5/8 x 5-3/8 x 1-5/8 in, 219 x 137 x 41 mm, 0.25 kg, rigid cardboard, standing on its 219 x 41 mm spine).
scoring: Evaluated over the end of the episode (SCORE_OVER = 'end', SUCCESS_HOLD_S = 1.0 s). 1.0: parcel fully inside the mailbox past the front sill (low_x >= 0.300 m), front door closed and latched (door_open_deg <= 3.0 deg), carrier signal flag upright (flag_angle_deg within 90.0 +/- 6.0 deg), both gripper TCPs at least 25 mm clear of the mailbox, door, flag, and parcel, and everything at rest for 1.0 s. 0.0 otherwise (no partial credit; parcel in and door shut with the flag down scores 0). Latched faults the robot must respect (nothing blocks them; the scorer records them and the score stays 0.0 for the rest of the episode): forcing the front door against the parcel at any door angle (door-parcel contact force > 15.0 N via PhysX RigidContactView; the catch alone presses a parcel resting against the closed door with under 1 N); or dropping the parcel off the table. Measured on real objects: sill clearance with a straightedge, door and flag angles with an inclinometer, door-parcel force with a force gauge or visible crushing, no visible dent in the box from the gripper, gripper clearance and the 1 s rest from a ruler and video.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lower the right-side carrier signal flag to 0 deg horizontal, swing the front door open to -82 deg, and place the USPS Small Flat Rate Box upright on its 219 x 41 mm spine at (0.260, +0.210, +0.0685 m).
fidelity: Mailbox (175 x 225 x 509 mm) and flat rate box (219 x 137 x 41 mm) are real size; the box mass is assumed. The mailbox is a fixed set of boxes. The door catch is a scripted drive: within 4 deg of closed a spring (0.016 N*m/deg, at most 0.14 N*m) draws the door shut and holds it until it is pulled past 9 deg; the flag detent snaps up past 68 deg. Not a real roller catch.
